title: Saturn Would Float in a Bathtub (If You Had One Big Enough)

scenes.text: Drop Saturn into a bathtub and it would float.
Saturn is huge. Ninety-five times the mass of Earth. Nine times wider.
But its average density is about zero point seven grams per cubic centimetre. Water is one. So Saturn is about thirty percent lighter than water, size for size.
It's the only planet in the solar system that can do this. Earth would sink like a stone. So would Jupiter.
That's because Saturn is mostly hydrogen and helium, the two lightest gases there are, puffed up into a ball of almost nothing.
The bathtub would need to be about a hundred and twenty thousand kilometres wide, though. Where would you put it?

description:
If you could find a bathtub big enough, Saturn would float in it.
Saturn has 95 times the mass of Earth, but its average density is only about 0.7 grams per cubic centimetre, about 30 percent less than water. It is the only planet in the solar system that is less dense than water.
That is because it is made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the two lightest elements, puffed up into an enormous ball.
The tub would need to be about 120,000 km wide. Where would you put it?
